value.rationale: The precise sharp inverse modulus estimate addresses a motivated quantitative gap in a 2026 general endpoint extension theorem. It treats an entire natural quartic moment-curve family for arbitrary admissible finite fields, supplies a strictly stronger coefficient than the prior all-degree bound, determines global optimizers of the deficit remainder, and identifies that the sharp global coefficient is forced by highly concentrated data, rather than by local curvature. This is not a mere alphabet-specific tabulation or routine restatement of uniform maximization.
